change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration raises when the `embed_category` setting row does not exist (every fresh DB)
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes the first row of the query. That query only returns a row when a `site_settings` row named `embed_category` exists and its value equals a category name. Settings are stored only when changed, so on a fresh install (`rake db:migrate` from scratch) and on any site that never set `embed_category`, the result is empty. `[0]` then fails (IndexError from `PG::Result#[]`, or NoMethodError on nil), and the whole migration aborts. The `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 is never reached in that case, so it is dead code. Line 15 has the same problem if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Check `cmd_tuples > 0` (as line 19 does) or use `.first`/`.to_a.first` and handle nil before reading the column.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw: full-URL values never match, and the SQL is unquoted
findings.body:
The old `embeddable_hosts` setting accepted entries such as `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`; the removed `allows_embeddable_host?` and its specs supported that. The raw `INSERT` bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path, so these values are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) compares `lower(host)` with the bare hostname, so those rows never match. After upgrading, embedding silently stops working for every site that used the scheme form, and the setting is deleted on line 31, so the original values are lost.

The same line interpolates `h` into the SQL unquoted. A `'` breaks the statement and aborts the migration. Blank lines and `\r` from `split("\n")` become empty or dirty hosts.

Normalise each entry before inserting: strip, drop blanks, remove `^https?://` and `/.*$`. Quote with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`.

findings.title: Irreversible data deletion in a `change` migration
findings.body: `change` creates the table (reversible) but also runs a raw `DELETE` on the old settings. Rolling back drops `embeddable_hosts` and the old settings are not restored, so the configured hosts are lost. Split into `up`/`down`, with `down` raising `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` or restoring the settings from the table. `create_table ... force: true` on line 3 also drops any existing `embeddable_hosts` table silently on a re-run.

findings.title: nil `host` raises NoMethodError in `before_validation`
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called without a nil check. `EmbeddableHost.new` (as in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create`) with a missing `host` param raises NoMethodError instead of failing the format validation, which gives an HTTP 500 rather than a JSON error. Guard with `self.host.try(:sub!, ...)`, or assign a stripped copy only when present.

findings.title: Host lookup ignores case of the referer and ignores ports, though the validator accepts ports
findings.body: The query lowercases the stored column but not the bound value, so a referer host in mixed case never matches. `uri.host` also never includes the port, while line 2 explicitly accepts `example.com:3000`. An admin can therefore save a host with a port and the embed will always be rejected, with no feedback. Either downcase `host` before the query and compare against `host:port` when a port is present, or drop the port from the format. `record_for_host` returns `false` or a record or nil, a mixed return type; callers only use `present?`/`try`, so returning nil consistently would be cleaner.

findings.title: Unknown id gives a 500 instead of a 404; missing params key also raises
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `where(id:).first` and then call methods on the possible nil (`host.destroy`, `host.host=`). A stale id (for example a host deleted in another tab) gives NoMethodError and a 500. Use `EmbeddableHost.find` / `raise Discourse::NotFound`. `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` on line 23 also raises if the key is absent. Line 24 stores whatever `category_id` is sent without checking that the category exists, and the DB column is NOT NULL with no foreign key. A bad id is saved, and `TopicEmbed.import` then passes it to `PostCreator`. Line 3 repeats the filters already inherited from `Admin::AdminController` (app/controllers/admin/admin_controller.rb:3-4).

findings.title: Delete failure is silent
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save` on line 40. If the server rejects or the request fails (for example the 404/500 above), nothing happens after the user confirms: no error and the row stays. Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)`.

findings.title: `saveChanges` action and the `update` endpoint are unused no-ops
findings.body: No template triggers `saveChanges` (templates/embedding.hbs has only `addHost`). It sends `update({})`, and `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9) saves nothing and just re-renders the object. The `PUT customize/embedding` route (config/routes.rb:139) and this action are dead code; remove them or implement them.

findings.title: `resources :embeddable_hosts` exposes routes with no actions
findings.body: The controller defines only create/update/destroy, but `resources` also routes index/show/new/edit, which fail with ActionNotFound. Add `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

findings.title: Plural hydration keeps `undefined` entries and `|| []` is dead
findings.body: `Array#map` always returns an array, so `hydrated || []` never applies. When an id is not found in the side-loaded collection, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined and the array holds `undefined` elements. The singular branch keeps the `_id` key in that case, but the plural branch always deletes `obj[k]`, so the ids are lost and consumers crash on `undefined`. Filter out falsy results, or keep the ids when anything is unresolved. This also changes behaviour for any `__rest_serializer` payload with a `*_ids` key, since the regex now matches them; I found only similar_topics and queued_posts using it, and did not check their payloads for `*_ids`.

findings.title: `find('fruit', 2)` is misleading and the plural case has no edge-case coverage
findings.body: The pretender `/fruits/:id` handler (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:226-228) ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]` (color_ids [1,2]). The test passes only because fruit 1's colors happen to have length 2, not because fruit 2 was loaded. Use id 1, or make the handler honour `:id`. There is also no test for a plural id missing from the side-loaded collection.

findings.title: Fabricator contents are in each other's files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, and the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This works only because all files in spec/fabricators are loaded. Git history for the category fabricators is lost and anyone looking for them will look in the wrong file. Swap the contents back so each file defines its own fabricator.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests that
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (app/models/topic.rb:869) no longer looks at embeddable hosts. This example now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed, so it duplicates the other cases under a false name. The `with an emeddable host` context (typo on line 1407) has no meaning either, because `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` does not affect the method under test. Remove the example, and drop the host from the context or rename both.

findings.title: New admin endpoints and migration have no behavioural tests
findings.body: Both new admin controller specs only assert the superclass. Nothing tests create/update/destroy (including invalid hosts, unknown ids, and non-staff access), the embedding `show` payload, or the data migration, which is where the defects above are. Add request-level specs for each action.

contracts.action: Run migration that creates embeddable_hosts, copies the old setting values and deletes the old settings rows
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts / embed_category read via SiteSetting; matching in the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? (app/models/site_setting.rb, removed lines)
contracts.before_after: Before: entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' were stripped of scheme at match time. After: the raw INSERT stores them verbatim, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares only against the bare hostname (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17), so scheme/path entries no longer match. On DBs with no embed_category row the first query result is empty and indexing [0] fails.
contracts.visible_effect: Upgrade aborts on fresh DBs; on upgraded sites that used scheme-prefixed entries embedding silently stops working.
contracts.failure_mode: Migration exception (fresh DB / no embed_category row); silent loss of matching with the original setting values deleted on line 31.

contracts.action: Delete: DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts','embed_category') in the migration
contracts.before_after: The delete targets fixed setting names, not records matched by a recorded id, so re-verification of identity is not applicable. It runs after the copy loop, and the copy loop uses un-normalised values, so the only copy of the data is the table of hosts that do not match.
contracts.visible_effect: Original host list is gone after upgrade; rollback restores nothing.
contracts.failure_mode: Not reversible; `change` rollback only drops the new table.

contracts.action: Admin deletes an embeddable host (confirm dialog, then destroyRecord)
contracts.before_after: The id sent is that of the clicked host. The server looks up by id and destroys it (embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15-16), removing one row only. With an unknown id, the nil host raises a 500. On success the component removes it from the list through sendAction('deleteHost').
contracts.visible_effect: Row disappears on success; on failure nothing is shown and the row stays.
contracts.failure_mode: Rejected promise from destroyRecord is not caught; the user gets no feedback.

contracts.action: Embed request authorisation now uses EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? plus the 'embeddable hosts not set' check
contracts.before_after: Before: blank setting rejected, then exact host match. After: no rows means host_allowed? is false, so it still rejects; matching uses lower(host) = uri.host, which is case-sensitive on the referer side and ignores ports. The development-admin bypass is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Embeds from hosts with a port or mixed-case referer are rejected.
contracts.failure_mode: Raises Discourse::InvalidAccess (rejected); the admin gets no hint why for host:port entries.

contracts.action: Load the admin Embedding page and render hosts hydrated from ids
contracts.equivalent_path: Other admin REST pages via store.find (e.g. adminPermalinks route)
contracts.before_after: store.find('embedding') -> EmbeddingAdapter.pathFor fixed to /admin/customize/embedding -> JSON with embedding.embeddable_host_ids and side-loaded embeddable_hosts -> Store._hydrateEmbedded turns the ids into an array of models. The data is loaded on each route entry (model hook), so returning to the page refetches.
contracts.visible_effect: Table of hosts and categories shown; empty list hides the table and shows only 'Add Host'.
contracts.failure_mode: A load failure is handled by Ember's route error handling. Unresolved ids give undefined array entries (store.js.es6:197-200).

summary: The migration is the main problem. It crashes when there is no `embed_category` setting row, which is every fresh DB. It also copies old hosts raw, so any entry written with `http://` or a path never matches `record_for_host`, and the old setting is deleted anyway. Smaller issues: nil-host and unknown-id 500s in the model and admin controller, case and port handling in the host lookup, an uncaught delete failure in the component, dead `saveChanges`/`update` code, and plural hydration that keeps `undefined` entries. The tests have several weaknesses: a stale-named topic_spec example, controller specs that only check the superclass, a store test that loads the wrong fruit, and category and embeddable_host fabricators defined in each other's files. I did not read or run the Ember or Rails code beyond the files cited.
